questions.question: What property guarantees that Kruskal's greedy edge choice is safe?
options: The cut property: the cheapest edge crossing any cut belongs to some MST
The existence of a topological order
questions.explanation: For any split of the vertices, the minimum crossing edge is in some MST, so adding the cheapest edge that does not form a cycle is always safe.

questions.question: For a complete graph on V points, which MST approach avoids building and sorting about V^2 / 2 edges?
questions.explanation: Array-based Prim scans vertices directly and can compute edge weights on the fly, running in O(V^2) without an explicit edge list.

questions.question: In Tarjan's bridge-finding, a tree edge u-v is a bridge when:
questions.explanation: low[v] > tin[u] means v's subtree cannot reach u or any ancestor without the edge u-v, so removing it disconnects the graph.

questions.question: In Kosaraju's algorithm, how is the second DFS pass run?
options: On the original graph, in vertex order
On the original graph, in finish order
On the reversed graph, in reverse finish order
On the reversed graph, in random order
questions.explanation: Processing vertices by decreasing finish time on the transposed graph makes each DFS collect exactly one SCC.
